newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SARB forward cover loss to fall from $20 bln-Stals.
newsitem.headline: SARB forward cover loss to fall from $20 bln-Stals.

text.p: The Reserve Bank's oversold forward foreign exchange position had risen to $20 billion but was likely to decline rapidly in 1997, central bank governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday.
He told a parliamentary media briefing that after climbing from $8 billion to $20 billion last year, the forward cover book was expected to start falling rapidly this year.

"The forward cover book is now declining and it is going to decline very sharply if the exchange rate remains stable and if there is the expectation that the exchange rate is going to continue to appreciate," Stals said.

"Nothing will happen with the foreign reserves. The exchange rate risk will be transferred back to the private sector. Even at the level of $20 billion we believe that there is a forward market outside the Reserve Bank of more or less the same amount.

Stals said he hoped that the Reserve Bank would be able to change the way in which it made forward cover available in the market in future. The book was managed on behalf of the Department of Finance and any losses were therefore borne by the taxpayer
Forward cover was not specifically provided to support the rand but to provide liquidity to the market.

Stals said the Reserve Bank started providing forward cover about three years ago but the central bank now wanted to "get rid of the forward cover facility, not in total, but we want to get to a situation where we will do forward cover as a normal comercial operation and not as a specific operation".
The increase in the forward cover book had been purely due to the fact that more South Africans are now taking out forward cover because they were concerned about the exchange rate.
